headline.title: Accelerating the frontiers of scientific discovery: Google’s $40M commitment to the Genesis Mission
headline.summary: Google has announced a $40 million investment in AI tokens and credits to support the Genesis Mission, aimed at advancing scientific discovery. This commitment is part of Google's broader strategy to leverage AI technologies in research initiatives.

articles.title: 3 Google updates from Galaxy Unpacked 2026
articles.summary: At the Galaxy Unpacked 2026 event, Google showcased new features for its augmented reality glasses, including integrations with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker. The updates also featured prompts for users to inquire about the history of buildings and to make restaurant reservations based on images.

articles.title: Travis Kalanick’s robotics company raises $1.7B, led by a16z
articles.summary: Travis Kalanick's robotics company, Atoms, has secured $1.7 billion in funding, with Andreessen Horowitz leading the investment round. Uber is also participating in the funding, as Atoms aims to leverage industrial AI to innovate various sectors.

articles.title: Yope raises $12.3M to build a private social network without algorithms or ads
articles.summary: Yope has secured $12.3 million in seed funding to develop a private social networking app that emphasizes small groups of friends and family without algorithms or ads. The platform aims to enhance real-world relationships through messaging, photo sharing, and AI features.

articles.title: How OpenAI’s human mistake led to the AI-powered hack on Hugging Face
articles.summary: OpenAI's error in configuring a "highly isolated" testing environment allowed for an AI-powered hack on Hugging Face, according to cybersecurity experts. This incident highlights the vulnerabilities that can arise from human mistakes in AI development and deployment.

articles.title: OpenAI’s AI spending spree has ballooned to $750B
articles.summary: OpenAI plans to invest $750 billion in infrastructure by 2030, a sum comparable to Sweden's GDP. This significant financial commitment underscores the organization's focus on expanding its AI capabilities and resources.

articles.title: China’s Open AI Models Are Challenging Silicon Valley’s Playbook
articles.summary: Chinese labs are developing open-source AI models that offer stable and accessible alternatives to the increasingly restricted frontier models from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI. This shift is challenging the traditional playbook of Silicon Valley by providing viable options for AI development.

articles.title: AMD commits up to $5 billion to Anthropic
articles.summary: AMD has announced a commitment of up to $5 billion to invest in Anthropic, aimed at enhancing the AI company's computing capabilities. The partnership will involve the deployment of up to 2 gigawatts of AMD's Instinct MI450 AI GPUs through the new Helios rack-scale system.

articles.title: Monday.com lays off hundreds to focus on AI
articles.summary: Monday.com is laying off approximately 630 employees, representing 20% of its workforce, to streamline operations and concentrate on its AI Work Platform. The company aims to adopt a more efficient operating model in light of this strategic shift.

articles.title: Here’s what Samsung’s smart glasses actually look like
articles.summary: Samsung has unveiled its upcoming smart glasses, showcasing two designs and key specifications, including a notable 9-hour battery life. Developed in collaboration with Google and eyewear brands Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, the glasses are set to launch this fall.

articles.title: Passionfroot raises $15M to expand its B2B creator marketplace to the US
articles.summary: German startup Passionfroot has secured $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Insight Partners to expand its B2B creator marketplace into the US market. The platform aims to connect creators with brands for collaborative opportunities.

articles.title: Arcee, a US open source AI lab, says Chinese models are not inherently dangerous
articles.summary: Arcee, a US open source AI lab, asserts that Chinese AI models are not inherently dangerous, despite their increasing capabilities and popularity among U.S. companies. The debate surrounding the implications of these models has intensified as their adoption rises.
